exposure: Mode of delivery of the second twin (vaginal, cesarean, or combined) after attempted vaginal delivery of the first twin
cohort: Women with dichorionic twin pregnancies attempting vaginal delivery over a 10-year period
finding: This study of women with dichorionic twin pregnancies found that while the second twin had significantly lower umbilical artery cord pH and Apgar scores compared to the first twin, these differences were not clinically significant.
mod_finding: Second twins born via cesarean section or combined delivery had significantly poorer outcomes compared to those born vaginally, although the clinical relevance of this finding was deemed negligible.
